beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A cheap individual response may belong to an expensive, unreliable trajectory.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A constrained workflow may outperform broader autonomy for a predictable recurring task.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The argument is comparative, not a rule that one pattern always wins.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Readers gain a way to discuss efficiency without hiding the human work around automation.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Those comparisons lead to the book's tension between flexibility and dependable control.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Hardcoded workflows can be predictable while struggling with changing or unfamiliar tasks.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Unrestricted autonomy can adapt while making behavior and cost harder to bound.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book explores intermediate designs that preserve choice within explicit operational limits.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: This is an engineering tradeoff to measure, rather than a slogan about maximum independence.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: It prepares readers to evaluate the concrete runtime proposals in the final movement.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The later chapters present ScriptaHubAgentLib and a proposed runtime called MRP-VM.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: These designs explore skill execution, controlled context, state, and responsibility within agent systems.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Their inclusion does not establish that they outperform every existing agent architecture.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book instead describes evaluation questions and limits that could challenge their value.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: That distinction separates reading an engineering proposal from accepting a product claim.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Return to the earlier failure and cost chapters when judging what these proposals add.
